definition: Media richness is the extent to which an online learning platform offers communication and media features that create a richer user experience. In this research context, it is treated as a technological aspect of the learning environment that relates to social presence and to whether users intend to keep using the platform.

reasons: The packet supports media richness as a technological-environment-related variable in online learning and links it to social presence and continuance intention, but it does not define it as the extent to which a platform offers communication and media features or as creating a richer user experience.
The definition adds an explanatory characterization of the construct that is not stated in the source text and goes beyond the packet’s support.

The definition claims that media richness is specifically “the extent to which an online learning platform offers communication and media features.” The provided packet discusses “three dimensions of media richness” but does not describe media richness in terms of communication/media features, so this part is not supported.

The definition says media richness “relates to social presence.” While the packet supports a mediating role of social presence between media richness and continuance intention, it does not explicitly frame media richness as generally “relating to” social presence in those terms; the definition is close, but the first (communication/media features) element is the main unsupported substantive claim.

The remaining elements about it being a technological-environment-related variable, involving social presence, and influencing users’ intention to keep using the platform are consistent with the packet (e.g., mediating role of social presence; antecedent of continuance intention/retention).
